title: Group Chat and Homecoming
premise: Edmund Okafor, a brilliant but withdrawn coder, runs an anonymous group chat account that has become the confessional heart of his senior class — until a college essay prompt asking 'What truth are you still carrying?' goes viral and classmates start answering with secrets that trace back to him. As Edmund races toward graduation, he must lead his underdog quiz-bowl team to a championship that could fund his future while untangling the anonymous identity he shares with Priya Raghavan, the girl he loves and the only person who might expose him. When the essay leak threatens to destroy friendships on the eve of both championships — academic and personal — Edmund chooses honesty over anonymity, confessing in front of the school at the final match. He loses the trophy but wins back the people he loves, learning that inheritance is not what we're given but what we choose to carry forward.
about_author: Bram Voss is the pen name of a former debate coach turned novelist who writes about overachievers quietly falling apart. They live in the Midwest with an aging dog and a group chat they can never leave.

chapters.title: The Account That Knows
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. We meet @grayarea, the anonymous group chat moderator whose careful curation holds his class's secrets. Edmund counts down 94 days to graduation like a prison sentence. Emotional beat: controlled detachment masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Prompt Number Four
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The college essay prompt 'What truth are you still carrying?' lands in English class, and answers begin leaking into the group chat overnight. Priya recognizes a detail only Edmund would know. Beat: suspicion kindling into curiosity.

chapters.title: Ninety-One Days
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Quiz-bowl captain Marcus drags Edmund onto the team as their last hope for regionals; the prize includes a scholarship Edmund secretly needs. Beat: reluctant commitment, duty pressing against desire.

chapters.title: What Priya Carries
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Her draft essay reveals her late mother's unfinished immigration petition — an inheritance of paperwork and grief she's never voiced aloud. She almost posts it anonymously. Beat: raw vulnerability.

chapters.title: Practice Round
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. First team practice is chaos; Edmund's cold efficiency alienates teammates but wins the scrimmage. Priya watches from the bleachers, testing him with a question only @grayarea could answer. Beat: masks slipping.

chapters.title: The Leak
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Someone screenshots three anonymous essays and pins them to the school forum. Friendships fracture; the group chat explodes. Edmund realizes one leaked secret is his own coded confession. Beat: panic, loss of control.

chapters.title: Seventy Days
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya confronts Edmund obliquely at the library, quoting his own post back to him. He deflects; she leaves her mother's petition file open on the table like bait. Beat: cat-and-mouse tenderness.

chapters.title: Regionals
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The team scrapes through regionals on a buzzer-beater answer about memory and inheritance — uncomfortably on-theme. Marcus celebrates; Edmund can't stop watching the door for Priya. Beat: hollow victory.

chapters.title: Two Truths
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya admits she knows he's @grayarea — or half of it. Edmund discovers she's been co-moderating a mirror account all along. Their anonymity was shared, and so is the danger. Beat: betrayal braided with relief.

chapters.title: Sixty Days
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund's father arrives unannounced, pushing a computer science future Edmund never chose, invoking family sacrifice. The scholarship stakes sharpen. Beat: suffocating duty versus selfhood.

chapters.title: The Petition
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya finds her mother's petition denied years ago; the family hid it to protect her focus. Grief curdles into anger aimed at everyone, including Edmund. Beat: inherited sorrow turning sharp.

chapters.title: State Semifinals
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The team advances, but Marcus discovers Edmund's scholarship motive and accuses him of using them. Team cohesion cracks before finals. Beat: guilt compounding.

chapters.title: What We Posted
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Edmund and Priya trace the leak to quiet teammate Dana, who posted the essays to force the school to confront its secrets. They must decide: expose her or protect her. Beat: moral crossroads.

chapters.title: Fifty Days
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya rewrites her college essay around the denial letter, choosing truth over polish. She asks Edmund what he'll do when the mask comes off. Beat: courage becoming contagious.

chapters.title: The Championship That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. State finals: the team plays beautifully and loses by five points. In defeat, Marcus forgives Edmund, and the team becomes real friends. Beat: losing the small prize, gaining something larger.

chapters.title: Forty-Nine Days
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund's father finds the @grayarea drafts on his laptop and reads them aloud at dinner — every secret, including Priya's. Beat: devastation; the last wall falls.

chapters.title: Silence in the Chat
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The group chat goes dark after the exposure. Classmates turn on Edmund; Priya defends him publicly, costing her a recommendation letter. Beat: love choosing sides against safety.

chapters.title: The One That Does
chapters.summary: Dual POV. With graduation nearing, Edmund and Priya realize the championship that matters is each other — and the community they broke and built. They plan a final post: no anonymity, just names. Beat: resolve hardening into hope.

chapters.title: Last Question
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. At the senior assembly, Edmund takes the microphone during the essay-prompt reading and answers honestly: what he carried, what he did with it, whom he hurt. Beat: public confession, terrifying and freeing.

chapters.title: Answers
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. One by one, classmates stand and finish their true essays — Dana first, then Marcus, then even Edmund's father, quietly, from the back row. Beat: collective catharsis.

chapters.title: Graduation Day
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Diplomas, the scholarship lost but a coding internship earned on merit, Priya's appeal filed with her mother's signature finally scanned. They delete the accounts together. Beat: release; inheritance reclaimed as choice.

chapters.title: Group Chat, Archived
chapters.summary: Dual POV epilogue. One year later, Edmund and Priya open a new chat with real names and invite the old members. The first message is the essay prompt, answered simply: 'I stayed.' Beat: love outlasting duty; memory carried forward.
